subject: health
title: Germs and Handwashing
about: How germs get in and around (hands, coughs, sneezes, shared cups, doorknobs) and the habits that stop them: soap for the length of the ABC song, scrubbing between fingers, drying, tissues in the trash, your own cup, and resting at home when sick. NC 1.PCH.1.1 (how germs cause illness and spread) and 1.PCH.1.2 (ways to stop them); builds on Healthy Habits for cold season.
tip: Rub a little lotion and glitter on his hands, then see how much soap and scrubbing it takes to get it all off; that is how germs hide.

cards.q: What song can you sing while you scrub your hands?
cards.note: The ABC song takes about 20 seconds. Happy Birthday two times works too.

cards.q: Where should you scrub when you wash your hands?
cards.note: Backs of hands, between fingers and under nails. Germs hide there.

cards.q: After you rinse, what do you do with your hands?
cards.a: dry them with a clean towel
cards.note: Wet hands pick up germs more easily, so dry them well.

cards.q: You just used the bathroom. What do you do next?
cards.note: Every time, even if you only went a little.

cards.q: You come inside after playing in the dirt. What do you do before snack?
cards.note: Also wash after petting an animal and after blowing your nose.

cards.q: You sneeze into a tissue. Where does the tissue go?
cards.note: Trash the tissue, then wash your hands.

cards.q: Why is your elbow a better place to cough than your hands?
cards.note: Germs on your hands get on everything you touch. Your elbow stays out of the way.

cards.q: Your friend wants a sip from your cup. What is a smart idea?
cards.note: Cups, spoons and straws carry germs from mouth to mouth.

cards.q: Which is a kind way to say hello without spreading germs?
cards.note: A wave, a smile or an elbow bump all work.

cards.q: Germs are too tiny to see. What tool do scientists use to see them?
cards.note: A microscope makes tiny things look big.

cards.q: Why do you stay home when you are sick?
cards.a: to rest and not share germs
cards.note: Rest helps your body fight the germs. Staying home keeps them away from your friends.

cards.q: Who gives you a checkup and a shot that helps your body fight germs?
cards.note: A shot is called a vaccine. It teaches your body to beat a germ before it makes you sick.

cards.a: touching your nose, then a toy
cards.note: Germs from your nose ride on your fingers to the toy, then to a friend.

cards.q: Your hands look clean. Can they still have germs on them?
cards.note: Germs are too small to see, so wash even when hands look clean.

cards.q: Sleep and healthy food help your body do what?
cards.note: A rested, well-fed body has a strong germ-fighting team inside.

cards.q: Where do germs hide at home that many hands touch?
cards.note: Remote controls, faucets and tablets too. Grown-ups wipe them clean.

cards.q: Germs get into your body through which places?
cards.note: Try not to touch your face with unwashed hands.
